title: VoltPilot Consumer Policy
description: The declarative operating requirements of ONE controllable consumer (steuerbarer Verbraucher), verbatim per docs/verbrauchssteuerung.md §10. A policy belongs to exactly one consumer entity (entity_id -> measurement_point). The requirements[] carry the four operating shapes (reactive / fixed_window / flexible_task / opportunistic). This schema pins the DOCUMENT shape; the rules JSON Schema cannot express (kind/enforcement coherence, must_run=>grid allow, condition-tree depth, cloud-vs-local signal hysteresis, catalog signal names, D4 power-range disjointness, 24:00 normalisation) live in consumer-policy-vectors.json and are enforced by the ConsumerPolicyValidator twins (Java services/api .../consumers/ConsumerPolicyValidator + TS frontend/portal/src/consumers/validate.ts), the FlowGraphValidator precedent. content_hash is derived server-side from canonical JSON and is NOT part of the document. schema_version starts at 1.0 (brand-new contract). Increment 1 (docs/verbrauchssteuerung.md §19): the policy is authored + stored as a DRAFT; no compiler, optimizer or edge command exists yet.

entity_id.description: The consumer entity this policy governs (registry measurement_point id or a stable external ref).

timezone.description: IANA zone of the site; time windows are authored in it and expanded to concrete UTC intervals by the cloud compiler (§5.2). v1 is effectively Europe/Berlin (existing pinning).

control_profile.description: OPTIONAL snapshot of the effective control profile the requirements were authored against (control_kind, rated power, stufen/ranges). Present so percent/kW targets and D4 power_ranges_kw are contract-checkable; the AUTHORITATIVE profile is the consumer_profile row (§9.2).

requirements.description: The operating requirements of this consumer, merged into ONE target at runtime (§7). Empty is not a policy.

id.description: Stable id for audit + fulfilment attribution (§10). Unique within the policy.

kind.description: reactive = target while a condition holds (§5.1/§5.3); fixed_window = target in a recurring local window (§5.2); flexible_task = a demand due by a deadline whose timing VoltPilot chooses (§5.4); opportunistic = run when energy is cheap/surplus, no obligation (§5.5).

enforcement.description: Verbindlichkeit (§5). must_run = Pflichtlauf (implies grid_energy_policy=allow, E2); required_by_deadline = flexible task; opportunistic = optional.

condition.description: reactive only: the boolean condition tree (§5.3).

recurrence.description: fixed_window / flexible_task: the recurring local window (§5.2/§5.4).

demand.description: flexible_task only: what must be done by the deadline (§5.4).

grid_energy_policy.description: Per-requirement override of the consumer default (§10). must_run forces allow. Absent = inherit the consumer default.

allow_storage_discharge.description: Per-requirement override (E10); absent = inherit the consumer default. Only meaningful at sites with storage.

service_rank.description: Conflict rank between mandatory consumers (§7); set only after a detected conflict. NEVER an edge arbitration class.

value.description: on_off => boolean; percent => 0..100; kw => >= 0; mode => a device mode string.

condition.description: A boolean condition tree (§5.3): a leaf, or an ANY/ALL/NOT group. Depth/size limits and the cloud-vs-local hysteresis rules are enforced by the validator.

signal.description: A signal name from the server catalog (ConsumerSignalCatalog). Unknown names are rejected by the validator (§10).

reset_value.description: Hysteresis reset threshold. ONLY local signals (SoC / PV-surplus / grid-flow) may carry it; cloud-compiled price/time signals must not (D1).

max_age_s.description: Freshness window for a LOCAL signal; a stale value is `unknown`, never 0 (§3.3). Cloud-compiled signals must not carry it (D1).

contiguous.description: true = one run block; false = splittable (§5.4/E5).

levels_kw.description: stepped only: the explicit level list (§4.3); must contain 0 and strictly ascend.

power_ranges_kw.description: continuous only, D4: disjoint, ascending [min,max] power ranges (e.g. 1- vs 3-phase charging), each within the effective rated power. The validator enforces disjointness + ordering + bounds; below the smallest minimum the consumer is off.
